correctness.rationale: The proof computes the exact singular-value distortion of a harmonic K-quasiregular differential, derives a regularized Laplacian comparison for |f| versus the Euclidean norm of the analytic components, and integrates it with Green's radial-mean identity. The center terms match because g(0)=0. This yields uniform H^1 control of h and g from the h^1 norm of f, hence an L^1 boundary trace. Applying the classical p=1 analytic Gabriel theorem to h and g gives the stated curve estimate. All zero sets are handled by epsilon-regularization and no finite experiment is used.

value.rationale: The fresh source explicitly asks which additional quasiregular assumptions restore a full Gabriel inequality at the excluded endpoint p=1. General harmonic h^1 fails there. The theorem supplies a natural central subclass, harmonic K-quasiregular maps, together with an explicit K-dependent boundary-to-curve estimate and automatic L^1 boundary trace. This closes the p=1 existence direction of the source problem for that class and is mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary specialization.
